title: Cliff Jackson's musical background and the school of Washington pianists
summary: He studied with teachers; pupils sent a delegate to lessons and passed on what they learned.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Cliff had quite a background on music. As I said before, he studied when he was quite young but he gave it up because he wanted to play jazz. And when he came to New York he told me the story about he and Fats Waller and James P. Johnson and Willie "the Lion" Smith -- stride pianist of that day, one of them would go to this German professor who taught them the fundamentals in harmony and theory and they all couldn't

afford to take lessons, so they would send a delegate, that would pay for the lessons and each studied the same method --
He'd come back with the good word.
That's right, so there was definitely a school of striving pianists in those days and Cliff was one of them.
